verdict.headline: The ten-year Treasury yield broke through 5% to its highest level since 2007
verdict.label: Ten-year rose three basis points to 5.02% and as high as 5.041%, clearing the 2023 peak for the highest print since 2007; thirty-year +7 bp to 5.40%, two-year +5 bp to 4.686%. Brent +1.77% to $107.55 and WTI +1.85% to $103.27 with Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline out for weeks. Dow futures -266 (-0.5%), S&P -28 (-0.4%), Nasdaq 100 -90 (-0.3%). Gold -0.84% to $4,263.19, bitcoin about $77,800 before a 2:15 p.m. Clarity Act cloture vote, September 16 hike priced near 92%
verdict.rationale_short:
The ten-year Treasury yield rose to 5.02% Tuesday morning and reached 5.041%, clearing the 2023 peak that held on Monday and printing its highest level since 2007. The committee meeting today had little to do with it: the September hike was already priced near 92%, which would take the target range to 3.75%-4.00%, and the Fed is in blackout, so no policy information arrived overnight. What distinguishes the move is where it sat on the curve. The thirty-year rose seven basis points to 5.40%, against the two-year's five and the ten-year's three, which concentrates the selling where inflation and issuance are priced rather than where the policy rate is. The two-year's five basis points are roughly what the shift in hike odds from 87% to 92% is worth; the thirty-year's seven are not.

The mechanism is an oil supply shock whose clock lengthened. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, shut on September 11 after drone strikes the day before damaged pumping stations, has put about 4 million barrels a day at risk — roughly 4% of global supply — and the kingdom could begin to exhaust oil available for export within days unless operations resume. Two regional officials told the Associated Press the line will be mostly out of service for weeks. That matters more than the outage itself: the pipeline was the workaround for the Hormuz blockade, so losing it removes the escape route rather than adding a second problem. Brent rose 1.77% to $107.55 and WTI 1.85% to $103.27, extending a gain of more than 21% over one month.

Equities are treating this as a rates problem rather than a growth one, for now. Dow futures were down 266 points or 0.5%, S&P 500 futures 28 points or 0.4%, and Nasdaq 100 futures 90 points or 0.3% — the growth-heavy index down least, which is not the ordering a duration shock normally produces and not what a continuing de-rating of AI hardware would look like after Monday's move. Gold fell 0.84% to $4,263.19 with EUR/USD at 1.1536, a third consecutive session of metals trading against the geopolitical narrative rather than with it, which reads as a real-rate and dollar effect overriding the safety bid. Bitcoin gave back 3% from an overnight $79,530 to about $77,800 ahead of a 2:15 p.m. ET Senate cloture vote on the Clarity Act, where 60 votes are needed and Republicans hold 53.

The evidence cuts both ways on how durable the break is. Against it: the move came overnight, in thinner trade, two sessions before a decision that is fully priced, and pre-decision hedging is a common reason a level gives way without holding. For it: Monday's rejection at 5.01% came from buyers appearing rather than from any input changing, and every input has since worsened. The levels that would settle it are a ten-year back under 4.90%, which would say the break was a hedge rather than a repricing, and a WTI settle under $100, which would say the supply premium is deflating on its own. The September Empire State manufacturing survey at 8:30 a.m. ET is the only US data before Wednesday; a weak print that fails to pull the ten-year back under 5% would say the long end is no longer trading on growth evidence.
verdict.lede_short: The ten-year Treasury yield reached 5.041% Tuesday, clearing the 2023 peak and printing its highest level since 2007 — with the Fed in blackout and Wednesday's hike already priced near 92%. The thirty-year moved seven basis points against the two-year's five, putting the selling where inflation is priced, and the cause is a Saudi pipeline outage now measured in weeks that removes about 4% of global supply. A ten-year back under 4.90% would say the break was a pre-decision hedge.

trade_setups.thesis: The yield cleared 5% overnight to 5.041%, its highest since 2007, having been rejected at 5.01% on Monday by buyers appearing rather than by any input changing. Every input has since worsened: the pipeline outage moved from days to weeks, Brent is above $107, and hike pricing firmed to 92%. What is forming is a test of whether 5% converts from a ceiling into a floor. The counter-evidence is that the break came overnight in thinner trade, two sessions before a fully priced decision, which is a common shape for pre-decision hedging rather than repricing.
trade_setups.entry: 5.00% is the level that defines it, with 4.90% below and the thirty-year's 5.44% 2007 peak above; 5.041% is the reference high and 5.40% the thirty-year print.
trade_setups.invalidation: A reclaim of 4.90% would say the break was a hedge into Wednesday. A ten-year holding above 5.00% through the projections would say the market has repriced the inflation path independent of the policy rate.
trade_setups.horizon: Wednesday September 16 through the end of the week

trade_setups.asset: The Saudi pipeline restart against the Fed's projections
trade_setups.thesis: The East-West line has been shut since September 11 and is described as out for weeks, putting roughly 4% of global supply at risk while the Hormuz blockade leaves no alternative route. If it is still down when the dot plot prints Wednesday, the committee publishes an inflation path over a supply shock with no known end date. The situation resolves on an engineering timetable rather than a policy one, which is what makes it difficult to price.
trade_setups.entry: The restart announcement is the observable; $100 on WTI and $105 on Brent are the levels that mark the premium deflating, against $103.27 and $107.55 now.
trade_setups.invalidation: A confirmed restart, or a Hormuz meeting receiving an actual date, would take crude back under $100 without any change in demand and remove the input driving the long end.
trade_setups.horizon: Days to five weeks, depending on repair scope

trade_setups.asset: The AI-safety rotation in its second session
trade_setups.thesis: Monday's move was large, one-sided and unaccompanied by any guidance change: Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike each rose more than 13% while CoreWeave fell about 8% and Oracle 4%. A narrative bid that survives a second session with no fresh catalyst has been underwritten; one that fades was confined to the headline that caused it. Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.3% against the Dow's 0.5% Tuesday is early evidence for the second reading, not the first.
trade_setups.entry: Monday's closing levels in the cybersecurity names are the reference; whether they hold without new news is the observable, alongside the Nasdaq's performance relative to the Dow.
trade_setups.invalidation: Cybersecurity giving back Monday's gains, or AI hardware recovering them, would say the move was a one-day crowd rather than a repricing of the capex cycle's duration.
